docs.text: T9 P1 设计记录：CSV 导入导出 + DATE/DECIMAL/BLOB 类型扩充 ¶ 目标 ¶ 在 P0（JOIN/GROUP BY/子查询/BETWEEN/IN/会话事务）基础上推进 P1： CREATE TABLE 列类型扩充为 INT / TEXT / DATE / DECIMAL / BLOB ，既有 INT/TEXT 行为不回归。 提供 EXPORT / IMPORT 两个 SQL 语句入口，实现表（或列子集）与 CSV 文件之间的往返导入导出。 类型系统全链路联动：比较（ compareVal ）、排序、索引键编码（ idxBytes ）、主键编码（ pkBytes ）、行编码（ encodeRow/decodeRow ）、WHERE 匹配、聚合（SUM/AVG）对新类型行为完整定义并实现。 新增/修改文件 ¶ 文件 变更 pkg/sql/value.go 新增：DATE 校验、DECIMAL 定点解析/规范化、BLOB hex 编解码、 coerceValue 、 decVal pkg/sql/ast.go 修改： Value.Kind / ColumnDef.Type 注释扩展；新增 ExportStmt / ImportStmt pkg/sql/lexer.go 修改：关键字表新增 EXPORT / IMPORT / TO ； lexNumber 支持小数 pkg/sql/parser.go 修改： parseStmt 分发 EXPORT/IMPORT； parseCreate 类型白名单扩展； parseValue 支持 DECIMAL 字面量；新增 parseExport / parseImport pkg/sql/executor.go 修改： Execute 分发； coerceRow 改用 coerceValue ； execUpdate SET 类型强制； doAgg / aggColumn 支持 DECIMAL 聚合； compareVal DECIMAL/BLOB 语义； indexLookup BLOB 索引列字面量解码 pkg/sql/meta.go 修改： idxBytes / pkBytes 支持 DECIMAL/BLOB； encodeRow / decodeRow 按新类型序列化 pkg/sql/csv.go 新增： execExport / execImport / parseCell / csvValue pkg/sql/sql.go 修改： IsSQL 关键字路由追加 EXPORT / IMPORT pkg/sql/sql_test.go 修改：新增 9 个 P1 用例（TestP1*） docs/T9_p1_csv_types.md 新增：本文档 README.md 修改：SQL subset、Highlights、Roadmap 勾选 P1 类型系统 ¶ 总览 ¶ 类型 内部形态 存储序列化（encodeRow） 主键/索引键字节 排序/比较语义 INT I int64 JSON number 定长 8B BE（主键原值 / 索引翻转符号位） 数值序 TEXT S string JSON string 原字节 字典序 DATE S string（ YYYY-MM-DD ） JSON string 原字节 字典序 = 时间序 DECIMAL I 缩放 int64（scale=4）+ S 规范化字符串 JSON string（规范化） 翻转符号位定长 8B 数值序（跨 INT 亦数值） BLOB S 大写 hex 文本 JSON string（大写 hex） hex 解码后的原始字节 原始字节序（hex 字符序 = 字节序） DATE ¶ 文本形态 YYYY-MM-DD ，插入/更新/导入时经 validateDate 做真实日历校验（含闰年）。 字典序即时间序，排序、索引键、主键直接使用原字节，无需额外编码。 非法值（格式错误、月份 13、2 月 30 日等）在 coerceValue / parseCell 阶段报错拒绝。 DECIMAL ¶ 定点数，固定小数位 scale=4 （ decUnit=10000 ）。 内部以 int64 缩放表示（ Value.I ），展示与存储用规范化字符串（ Value.S ，如 123.4500 ）。 输入接受 [-+]?digits[.digits] ：整数自动补 4 位小数；小数位超过 4 位报错（不截断不四舍五入）；超出 int64 缩放范围报错。 比较语义：DECIMAL 与 DECIMAL / INT 一律数值序（ compareDec ，INT 放大到 scale 后比较，避免溢出采用商/余两段比较）。 聚合： SUM / AVG 支持 DECIMAL 列，累加/平均以缩放整数进行，结果保持 4 位小数精度；空表 AVG 返回 0.0000 。INT 与 DECIMAL 混聚时按 DECIMAL 输出。 BLOB ¶ 二进制大对象；SQL 与 CSV 的输入输出形态均为 大写十六进制文本 （如 0AFF 、 DEADBEEF ）。 encodeRow 存大写 hex 字符串； decodeRow 还原为 BLOB Value。 主键/索引键编码为 hex 解码后的原始字节； pkBytes 在主键列为 BLOB 时，对 WHERE 字面量（TEXT 形态）统一按 hex 解码，保证点查与存储键一致； indexLookup 同理对 BLOB 索引列字面量先解码再编码。 比较语义：BLOB 与 BLOB 按解码后原始字节比较；BLOB 与 TEXT 比较时，TEXT 侧若为合法 hex 亦解码后比较（宽松匹配，例如 WHERE data = 'deadbeef' 命中存储 DEADBEEF ）。 类型强制（coerceValue） ¶ 列类型 接受输入 拒绝 INT INT 其余全部 TEXT TEXT / DATE（归一为 TEXT） INT / DECIMAL / BLOB DATE DATE / 合法 YYYY-MM-DD 文本 其余 DECIMAL DECIMAL / INT / 合法数字文本 其余 BLOB BLOB / 合法 hex 文本 其余 CSV 导入导出 ¶ 语法 ¶ EXPORT TABLE t [(col, ...)] TO 'path' IMPORT INTO t FROM 'path' EXPORT TABLE t TO 'path' ：导出表全部列。 EXPORT TABLE t (a, c) TO 'path' ：导出列子集（按给定列序）。 IMPORT INTO t FROM 'path' ：从 CSV 文件导入建行。 CSV 规范（RFC 4180 风格） ¶ UTF-8 文本； 首行为表头 （列名，与表定义顺序一致），后续每行为一条记录。 字段含逗号/双引号/换行时以双引号包裹，内部双引号翻倍（ "" ），由 Go encoding/csv 保证。 各类型字段文本形态： INT：十进制整数 TEXT：原样（含空串） DATE： YYYY-MM-DD DECIMAL：十进制数（导出为规范化 4 位小数；导入接受 ≤4 位小数） BLOB：大写十六进制（导入大小写均可） 导出行为 ¶ 表内行按主键序导出（存储序）。 导出文件为 UTF-8 无 BOM；表头 = 导出的列名。 文件写入在事务读快照之后进行，路径不存在时自动创建，覆盖已有文件（同名覆盖由调用方负责确认）。 导入行为（原子语义） ¶ 单事务执行：任一行的列数不匹配 / 类型非法 / 表头不符 → 整体报错回滚，不产生部分写入。 主键重复的行跳过 （不覆盖、不报错），返回 inserted / skipped 两列计数。 表头列名与表定义顺序必须完全一致（顺序敏感，简单明确）。 设计取舍 ¶ 选择 EXPORT/IMPORT 而非标准 COPY ：与既有 DDL/DML 关键字风格一致，避免 COPY 与复制语义歧义。 首行强制表头：导入自描述、可校验列序，避免按位置猜测。 DECIMAL 采用 int64 缩放（scale=4）：实现简单、比较/索引友好、无浮点误差；代价是范围受限（±9.2e14 缩放值）与固定小数位，文档明确即可。 BLOB 文本 hex：SQL 子集无二进制字面量，hex 文本与既有字符串 lexer 天然兼容。 主键重复跳过而非报错：导入常用语"灌数据"，跳过幂等重放，配合原子性保证不脏写。 验证 ¶ 新增 9 个 P1 用例（ pkg/sql/sql_test.go ， TestP1* ）： TestP1CreateInsertNewTypes — 新类型建表 + 插入 + 查询 TestP1DateValidation — DATE 合法/非法边界 TestP1DecimalCompareOrder — DECIMAL 比较与排序 TestP1DecimalAgg — DECIMAL SUM/AVG 聚合（含空表） TestP1BlobRoundtrip — BLOB 存取/点查/比较往返 TestP1CsvExportImportRoundtrip — 导出→导入往返一致性 TestP1CsvExportColumns — 列子集导出 TestP1CsvImportSemantics — 表头/列数/主键重复/类型错误语义 TestP1MixedTypesWithIndex — 混合类型建索引 + 范围查询 全仓 go test ./... -count=1 全绿（本机真实 CGO 工具链）。 （内容由AI生成，仅供参考）

docs.text: 类型 内部形态 存储序列化（encodeRow） 主键/索引键字节 排序/比较语义 INT I int64 JSON number 定长 8B BE（主键原值 / 索引翻转符号位） 数值序 TEXT S string JSON string 原字节 字典序 DATE S string（ YYYY-MM-DD ） JSON string 原字节 字典序 = 时间序 DECIMAL I 缩放 int64（scale=4）+ S 规范化字符串 JSON string（规范化） 翻转符号位定长 8B 数值序（跨 INT 亦数值） BLOB S 大写 hex 文本 JSON string（大写 hex） hex 解码后的原始字节 原始字节序（hex 字符序 = 字节序）
docs.title: 总览

docs.text: 文本形态 YYYY-MM-DD ，插入/更新/导入时经 validateDate 做真实日历校验（含闰年）。 字典序即时间序，排序、索引键、主键直接使用原字节，无需额外编码。 非法值（格式错误、月份 13、2 月 30 日等）在 coerceValue / parseCell 阶段报错拒绝。
docs.title: DATE

docs.text: 定点数，固定小数位 scale=4 （ decUnit=10000 ）。 内部以 int64 缩放表示（ Value.I ），展示与存储用规范化字符串（ Value.S ，如 123.4500 ）。 输入接受 [-+]?digits[.digits] ：整数自动补 4 位小数；小数位超过 4 位报错（不截断不四舍五入）；超出 int64 缩放范围报错。 比较语义：DECIMAL 与 DECIMAL / INT 一律数值序（ compareDec ，INT 放大到 scale 后比较，避免溢出采用商/余两段比较）。 聚合： SUM / AVG 支持 DECIMAL 列，累加/平均以缩放整数进行，结果保持 4 位小数精度；空表 AVG 返回 0.0000 。INT 与 DECIMAL 混聚时按 DECIMAL 输出。
docs.title: DECIMAL

docs.text: 二进制大对象；SQL 与 CSV 的输入输出形态均为 大写十六进制文本 （如 0AFF 、 DEADBEEF ）。 encodeRow 存大写 hex 字符串； decodeRow 还原为 BLOB Value。 主键/索引键编码为 hex 解码后的原始字节； pkBytes 在主键列为 BLOB 时，对 WHERE 字面量（TEXT 形态）统一按 hex 解码，保证点查与存储键一致； indexLookup 同理对 BLOB 索引列字面量先解码再编码。 比较语义：BLOB 与 BLOB 按解码后原始字节比较；BLOB 与 TEXT 比较时，TEXT 侧若为合法 hex 亦解码后比较（宽松匹配，例如 WHERE data = 'deadbeef' 命中存储 DEADBEEF ）。
docs.title: BLOB

docs.text: 列类型 接受输入 拒绝 INT INT 其余全部 TEXT TEXT / DATE（归一为 TEXT） INT / DECIMAL / BLOB DATE DATE / 合法 YYYY-MM-DD 文本 其余 DECIMAL DECIMAL / INT / 合法数字文本 其余 BLOB BLOB / 合法 hex 文本 其余
docs.title: 类型强制（coerceValue）

docs.text: EXPORT TABLE t [(col, ...)] TO 'path' IMPORT INTO t FROM 'path' EXPORT TABLE t TO 'path' ：导出表全部列。 EXPORT TABLE t (a, c) TO 'path' ：导出列子集（按给定列序）。 IMPORT INTO t FROM 'path' ：从 CSV 文件导入建行。
docs.title: 语法

docs.text: UTF-8 文本； 首行为表头 （列名，与表定义顺序一致），后续每行为一条记录。 字段含逗号/双引号/换行时以双引号包裹，内部双引号翻倍（ "" ），由 Go encoding/csv 保证。 各类型字段文本形态： INT：十进制整数 TEXT：原样（含空串） DATE： YYYY-MM-DD DECIMAL：十进制数（导出为规范化 4 位小数；导入接受 ≤4 位小数） BLOB：大写十六进制（导入大小写均可）
docs.title: CSV 规范（RFC 4180 风格）

docs.text: 表内行按主键序导出（存储序）。 导出文件为 UTF-8 无 BOM；表头 = 导出的列名。 文件写入在事务读快照之后进行，路径不存在时自动创建，覆盖已有文件（同名覆盖由调用方负责确认）。
docs.title: 导出行为

docs.text: 单事务执行：任一行的列数不匹配 / 类型非法 / 表头不符 → 整体报错回滚，不产生部分写入。 主键重复的行跳过 （不覆盖、不报错），返回 inserted / skipped 两列计数。 表头列名与表定义顺序必须完全一致（顺序敏感，简单明确）。
docs.title: 导入行为（原子语义）

docs.text: 选择 EXPORT/IMPORT 而非标准 COPY ：与既有 DDL/DML 关键字风格一致，避免 COPY 与复制语义歧义。 首行强制表头：导入自描述、可校验列序，避免按位置猜测。 DECIMAL 采用 int64 缩放（scale=4）：实现简单、比较/索引友好、无浮点误差；代价是范围受限（±9.2e14 缩放值）与固定小数位，文档明确即可。 BLOB 文本 hex：SQL 子集无二进制字面量，hex 文本与既有字符串 lexer 天然兼容。 主键重复跳过而非报错：导入常用语"灌数据"，跳过幂等重放，配合原子性保证不脏写。
docs.title: 设计取舍

docs.text: ADR-004: 存储引擎选型——RocksDB（M1, v2.0-FP） ¶ 日期：2026-10-07 状态：已接受 决策者：OpenXDB 项目（M0-lite 实验结论 → M1 正式开发） 关联实验： E1 存储引擎基准实验记录 背景 ¶ M0-lite 阶段需为 OpenXDB 选定单机存储引擎。候选两条路线： RocksDB （C++，经 cgo 静态链接桥接入 Go） 自研内存 B+Tree （纯 Go， pkg/storage/btree ） 项目定位：教学/实验性质的单机关系型数据库内核，最终演进为分布式数据库；商用目标为技术招牌 + 内容 + 代运维载体。 决策标准 ¶ 标准 权重 说明 持久化与崩溃恢复 高 数据库内核的第一性需求，WAL 之外的最终落盘保障 成熟度与稳定性 高 商用招牌必须可对外演示，不能频繁丢数据 维护成本 中 单开发者项目，构建链路越简单越好 吞吐表现 中 实测数据支撑，但不单独决定选型 演进式开源路线 中 从单机长出来的分布式数据库：LSM/分区/SST 复用潜力 Go 主体 低 教学价值：核心逻辑仍以 Go 编写，cgo 仅限存储桥 备选方案评估 ¶ A. RocksDB（cgo 桥） ¶ 吞吐（E1a，100 万 key，未开 fsync）：顺序写 961,538 TPS / 随机写 186,498 TPS / 随机读 71,003 QPS（P99 60 us）。 持久化：SST + MANIFEST + WAL，自带崩溃恢复与压缩。 成熟度：生产级引擎，社区与文档完善。 代价：cgo 构建复杂（Windows 静态链接需 -lshlwapi -lrpcrt4 -lws2_32 ，C++20）；维护一层薄 C++ 桥（ pkg/storage/rocksdb ）。 B. 纯 Go 内存 B+Tree ¶ 吞吐（E1b，同口径）：顺序写 1,043,841 TPS / 随机写 406,339 TPS / 随机读 613,497 QPS（P99 0 us）。随机读快近 9 倍。 持久化：无。需自行实现落盘、恢复、WAL 复用，且内存结构上限决定数据规模受限。 维护成本：纯 Go 低，但自研数据结构正确性风险高（本轮已修复 merge/borrowLeft 两个不变量缺陷）。 C. 纯 Go LSM（Pebble 类） ¶ 吞吐与持久化均衡，社区成熟；但引入第三方 Go 引擎会削弱"从零实现"的教学价值，且未来分片/复制仍需抽象适配。 决策 ¶ 采用 RocksDB（cgo 静态链接）作为 OpenXDB 的存储引擎。 理由： 持久化与崩溃恢复不可妥协 ：B+Tree 吞吐优势（随机读 8.6 倍）本质来自"不落盘"，无法弥补数据库最基本的数据安全承诺；RocksDB 的 SST/MANIFEST 体系直接满足恢复需求。 成熟度支撑商用目标 ：生产级引擎可对外演示与代运维背书，自研存储的崩溃风险不适合作为招牌。 演进路线复用 ：RocksDB 的 LSM/SST/分区能力与"单机长出来的分布式数据库"路线天然衔接，M2 复制 / M3 分片可在存储层之上叠加，无需重写引擎。 教学价值保留 ：Go 侧保持存储抽象（ storage.Storage ）、Key 编码、事务、SQL 全部自研；cgo 桥仅封装 Put/Get/Scan/WriteBatch/Snapshot，职责边界清晰；B+Tree 保留为对照参考与内存引擎实验。 后果 ¶ 正向： 开箱即得的落盘、压缩、缓存与成熟恢复机制。 基准数据可直接进 README/博文，增强技术招牌说服力。 负向： 构建依赖 C/C++ 工具链与 RocksDB 静态库，Windows 下需固定英文路径工具链。 cgo 桥需随 RocksDB API 演进维护（如 v11 DB::Open 改 unique_ptr ）。 B+Tree 对照引擎保留在 pkg/storage/btree ，仅供实验，不承担生产路径。 参考 ¶ E1 存储引擎基准实验记录 （E1a RocksDB / E1b B+Tree） 首发博文：《为什么 OpenXDB 选 RocksDB》 （内容由AI生成，仅供参考）

docs.text: 备份调度与远程备份（BR 方向②） ¶ 本文档说明 OpenXDB 的备份调度与远程备份能力：周期自动 BACKUP、保留份数、 状态查询，以及 HTTP 远程备份（push/pull）与恢复路径。 1. 备份调度 ¶ 1.1 配置项（SET PERSIST 热更新，默认全部关闭） ¶ 配置键 默认 说明 backup_interval 0 调度周期（秒）。正整数开启周期自动 BACKUP； 0 关闭 backup_keep 0 保留份数。 N>0 仅保留最近 N 份调度备份； 0 不清理 backup_dir 空 调度备份输出目录；空=未配置（不执行调度备份） backup_remote_url 空 远程 HTTP PUT 上传目标；空=不上传 配置经现有 SET PERSIST 体系即时生效并落盘，重启后保留；也可在 cmd start 启动时通过命令行装配： openxdb start --data-dir <dir> \ --backup-interval 3600 \ --backup-keep 7 \ --backup-dir <dir>/backups \ --backup-remote-url http://127.0.0.1:8090/backups 启动未配置调度时默认目录为 <data>/backups （ --backup-dir 缺省值）。 1.2 状态查看 ¶ SHOW BACKUP STATUS; 返回调度配置（周期/保留份数/目录/远程目标）与最近执行状态 （下次执行时间/最近结果/最近错误）。 1.3 行为 ¶ 调度器在每个周期触发一次引擎级 BACKUP ，产物写入 backup_dir 。 每个周期触发前清理旧备份： backup_keep > 0 时仅保留最近 N 份。 备份完成后若配置了 backup_remote_url ，自动将备份文件 HTTP PUT 上传至远程。 db.Close 会停止调度循环，避免关闭过程中误触发 BACKUP。 2. 远程备份（HTTP） ¶ 远程备份基于现有网络栈实现为 HTTP 传输，至少支持两类目标： - 支持 HTTP PUT/GET 的自建端点（如 WebDAV 或自定义备份服务）。 2.1 push：上传本地备份到远程 ¶ openxdb backup push --file <local-backup-file> --url http://127.0.0.1:8090/backups/<name> 将本地备份文件上传至远程目标（HTTP PUT， --file 指定本地文件， --url 为完整远程目标 URL）。 2.2 pull：从远程下载备份到本地 ¶ openxdb backup pull --url http://127.0.0.1:8090/backups/<name> --out <local-path> 从远程目标下载备份到本地（HTTP GET， --url 为完整远程文件 URL， --out 为本地保存路径；先写 .tmp 再 rename，避免半文件被误用）。 3. 恢复路径 ¶ 远程备份的恢复路径： openxdb backup pull <remote-file> ... 将远程备份下载到本地目录； 使用现有恢复命令还原： RESTORE FROM '<local-downloaded-backup>'; 或按仓库现有 RESTORE/PITR 流程从下载的备份文件恢复。调度产生的本地备份 （ backup_dir 下）也可直接 RESTORE FROM '<backup_dir>/<file>' 恢复。 4. 与既有能力的关系 ¶ 复用现有 BACKUP / RESTORE 语句与引擎快照导出/物理恢复路径，调度器仅负责 周期性触发与保留清理。 SHOW BACKUP STATUS 与 SHOW CONFIG 同为只读状态查询，语法风格一致 （BACKUP/STATUS 按文本匹配兼容关键字表）。 远程传输仅使用标准库 HTTP client，不引入外部依赖。

docs.text: 为什么 OpenXDB 选 RocksDB：一次存储引擎选型的真实实验 ¶ OpenXDB 首发博文 | 2026-10-07 | github.com/zhengkuanhua/openxdb 从零写数据库，第一关就是存储引擎 ¶ OpenXDB 的目标是从零写一个单机关系型数据库内核，再慢慢长成分布式数据库。存储引擎是地基，选错后面全得返工。在动手前，我们做了一次真实基准实验（E1），把两条候选路线摆在桌面上： RocksDB ：生产级 LSM 存储引擎，通过一层薄薄的 cgo 桥接入 Go。 自研内存 B+Tree ：纯 Go 手写，作为"完全掌控"的对照。 实验：100 万 key，同口径对决 ¶ 两条路跑同一套基准：顺序写、随机写、随机读（批量 1000、单线程、记录 P99 延迟）。 场景 RocksDB B+Tree（内存） 倍率 顺序写 961,538 TPS 1,043,841 TPS 1.09x 随机写 186,498 TPS 406,339 TPS 2.18x 随机读 71,003 QPS（P99 60us） 613,497 QPS（P99 0us） 8.64x 内存 B+Tree 完胜，随机读快了将近 9 倍。数据这么好看，为什么还是选了 RocksDB？ 吞吐不是全部：快 9 倍的那台引擎，不落盘 ¶ 答案藏在实验条件里—— B+Tree 是纯内存结构 。它的"快"来自不写磁盘：没有 fsync、没有 SST、没有 MANIFEST。数据库的第一性需求是什么？是 数据不丢 。一个不落盘的引擎，进程一崩数据全没，吞吐再高也没法当数据库用。 RocksDB 的价值恰恰在看不见的地方： SST + MANIFEST ：数据落盘、元数据可恢复，崩溃后自动找回一致性； 成熟稳定 ：生产级引擎，压缩、缓存、合并策略久经考验； 演进衔接 ：LSM 的 SST/分区能力，天然适配"从单机长出来的分布式数据库"——M2 复制、M3 分片可以在存储层之上叠加，不用推翻重写。 而自研 B+Tree 的正确性风险，我们也真实踩到了：调试过程中修复了两个破坏树不变量的缺陷（内部节点 merge 漏插分隔键、borrowLeft 取错分隔键）。这正是教学实验的价值——但作为对外招牌，不能拿它当生产地基。 选型结论：全都要 ¶ 最终方案不是二选一： 存储主路径走 RocksDB （cgo 静态链接），把持久化、恢复、压缩这些"脏活"交给生产级引擎； 自研 B+Tree 保留 ，作为对照参考引擎、内存引擎实验与数据结构教学素材； Go 侧保持自研：存储抽象、Key 编码、WAL、事务、SQL 引擎全部从零实现，cgo 桥只封装最小读写接口。 留给你的话 ¶ 如果你的项目也是"从零写数据库"，请记住这次实验的教训： 基准数据要真实跑，但选型决策要看第一性需求 。B+Tree 快 9 倍是事实，可它不落盘也是事实。数据库的地基不是跑分，是数据安全。 OpenXDB 的完整实验记录、实现文档与源码都在 GitHub，欢迎 star、提 issue，一起把它从单机长成分布式。 （内容由AI生成，仅供参考）

docs.text: BR / PITR 自动化演练（br_pitr_drill） ¶ 概述 ¶ 针对 OpenXDB 已实现的备份恢复能力，提供一键可复现的端到端自动化演练： BR（全量备份与恢复） ： BACKUP TO '<path>' / RESTORE FROM '<path>' ，含灾难恢复闭环； PITR（时间点恢复） ： RESTORE FROM '<path>' TO LSN <n> ，基于 binlog 精确回放到备份点之后的任意提交位点。 演练包含完整的数据校验断言（行数、首末行、LSN 边界内外泄漏检查），任何一步失败即终止并返回失败点描述。相关实现见 pkg/sql/backup.go ，设计说明见 docs/T18_backup_restore.md 。 位置 ¶ 内容 路径 演练主程序（独立 main） tests/bench/br_pitr_drill/main.go 端到端测试（复用主流程） tests/bench/br_pitr_drill/drill_test.go 演练输出报告 -out 指定的 Markdown 文件（默认 br_pitr_drill_report.md ） 风格沿用 tests/bench/sql_bench 的独立 main 程序约定：flag 参数、 db.Init + db.Open 、 e.Execute 执行 SQL、Markdown 报告输出。 一键运行 ¶ # 先注入 RocksDB CGO 环境（本仓库 Windows 构建前提） .\scripts\build.ps1 -SkipAllBuild # 方式一：端到端测试（推荐，临时数据目录，默认数据量） go test ./tests/bench/br_pitr_drill/ -count=1 -v # 方式二：手动运行演练（自选数据量与输出路径） go run ./tests/bench/br_pitr_drill -dir "D:\tmp\brdrill-data" -backup "D:\tmp\brdrill.bak" -rows 1000 -pitr-rows 10 -out "D:\tmp\brdrill_report.md" 参数说明（方式二） ¶ 参数 默认 说明 -dir brdrill-data 演练数据目录（RocksDB + WAL + binlog） -backup brdrill.bak 备份文件输出路径 -rows 500 阶段 A 写入的基线行数 -pitr-rows 8 阶段 C/D 备份点后写入行数 -out br_pitr_drill_report.md 演练报告输出路径 演练闭环（A → D） ¶ A. 准备 ¶ 建表 drill_users ，写入 -rows 行基线数据（id 自 1 递增）。 B. 全量备份（BR 起点） ¶ BACKUP TO '<backup>' ，校验备份结果行数与基线一致、 backup_lsn > 0 。 C. PITR 精确回放 ¶ 备份点后逐条写入 -pitr-rows 行，记录每条提交后的 binlog LSN； 选取中间与末尾若干 LSN 作为检查点，逐个执行 RESTORE FROM '<backup>' TO LSN <n> ； 每个检查点校验：行数 = 基线 + 已回放条数、末行存在、超出 LSN 的行不存在（无泄漏）； TO LSN = backup_lsn （备份点本身）时，结果应恰为基线快照。 D. BR 灾难恢复闭环 ¶ 模拟灾难：备份点后写入数据并 DROP TABLE （误删/损坏场景）； RESTORE FROM '<backup>' 全量恢复； 校验行数等于基线、id=1 与 id=rows 均存在。 校验断言清单 ¶ 阶段 断言 B 备份返回 1 行；rows 与基线一致；backup_lsn > 0 C 每个 TO LSN 检查点行数精确；末行在、越界行无泄漏 C TO LSN = backup_lsn 时行数恰为基线，无备份点后数据 D 恢复后行数 = 基线；首行/末行存在 输出报告 ¶ 演练完成后输出 Markdown 报告（默认 br_pitr_drill_report.md ），包含： 演练时间、参数与通过/失败结论； 各阶段（A/B/C/D）执行步骤与校验结果； 备份文件信息（tables / rows / backup_lsn）； PITR 检查点 LSN 与校验明细。 约束与说明 ¶ 演练使用真实 RocksDB、WAL 与 binlog 链路（无 mock），可验证 pkg/sql/backup.go 与 server 命令入口的完整行为； drill_test.go 以 t.TempDir() 创建临时数据目录、较小数据量（50/6）快速回归，不污染仓库工作区； 仓库构建/测试前提：Windows + RocksDB CGO 环境，先执行 scripts/build.ps1 （或 -SkipAllBuild 仅注入环境）。

docs.text: BACKUP TO '<backup>' ，校验备份结果行数与基线一致、 backup_lsn > 0 。
docs.title: B. 全量备份（BR 起点）

docs.text: 备份点后逐条写入 -pitr-rows 行，记录每条提交后的 binlog LSN； 选取中间与末尾若干 LSN 作为检查点，逐个执行 RESTORE FROM '<backup>' TO LSN <n> ； 每个检查点校验：行数 = 基线 + 已回放条数、末行存在、超出 LSN 的行不存在（无泄漏）； TO LSN = backup_lsn （备份点本身）时，结果应恰为基线快照。
docs.title: C. PITR 精确回放

docs.text: 模拟灾难：备份点后写入数据并 DROP TABLE （误删/损坏场景）； RESTORE FROM '<backup>' 全量恢复； 校验行数等于基线、id=1 与 id=rows 均存在。
docs.title: D. BR 灾难恢复闭环

docs.text: 阶段 断言 B 备份返回 1 行；rows 与基线一致；backup_lsn > 0 C 每个 TO LSN 检查点行数精确；末行在、越界行无泄漏 C TO LSN = backup_lsn 时行数恰为基线，无备份点后数据 D 恢复后行数 = 基线；首行/末行存在
docs.title: 校验断言清单

docs.text: 演练完成后输出 Markdown 报告（默认 br_pitr_drill_report.md ），包含： 演练时间、参数与通过/失败结论； 各阶段（A/B/C/D）执行步骤与校验结果； 备份文件信息（tables / rows / backup_lsn）； PITR 检查点 LSN 与校验明细。
docs.title: 输出报告

docs.text: 演练使用真实 RocksDB、WAL 与 binlog 链路（无 mock），可验证 pkg/sql/backup.go 与 server 命令入口的完整行为； drill_test.go 以 t.TempDir() 创建临时数据目录、较小数据量（50/6）快速回归，不污染仓库工作区； 仓库构建/测试前提：Windows + RocksDB CGO 环境，先执行 scripts/build.ps1 （或 -SkipAllBuild 仅注入环境）。

docs.text: OpenXDB Product Manual (English) ¶ Version: v1.0.0 Last updated: 2026-10-16 Positioning: single-node edge benchmark relational database kernel. All features and data in this manual are based on real content from README.md and docs/ design documents — no fabricated parameters, numbers, or commands. Table of Contents ¶ Product Overview & Positioning Quick Start Installation & Deployment SQL Reference Client Drivers Data Security Operations & Observability Distributed Capabilities Performance Benchmark Known Limitations & Boundaries FAQ 1. Product Overview & Positioning ¶ OpenXDB is a from-scratch single-node/distributed relational database kernel written in Go, with a storage engine built on top of RocksDB (accessed through a thin cgo bridge). The kernel fully includes WAL (write-ahead log), transactions, SQL parsing & execution, replication, sharding, 2PC, HA (high availability), backup & restore — evolving from a learning/experimentation kernel into one with complete distributed capabilities. 1.1 Positioning Boundaries ¶ OpenXDB speaks a self-developed binary TCP protocol ( pkg/server ) and is not a MySQL wire protocol implementation. It therefore cannot directly interoperate with MySQL ecosystem tools (e.g., standard sysbench, mysqldump beyond the built-in import, binlog tools). Performance positioning is single-node edge benchmark : the kernel implements the full functional chain, and performance optimization is still ongoing; measured throughput is presented in Chapter 9 . OpenXDB does not position itself against TiDB, TDSQL, or MySQL. It is an independently implemented kernel for learning, experimentation, and edge scenarios. 1.2 Core Capabilities ¶ Capability Description Storage engine RocksDB-backed KV storage (cgo bridge pkg/storage/rocksdb ) + pure-Go in-memory B+Tree ( pkg/storage/btree , reference implementation & comparator) WAL Append-only write-ahead log with replay recovery ( pkg/wal ) Transactions Local ACID transactions with snapshot isolation; read-your-writes merge, tombstones, point/range scan ( pkg/txn ) SQL subset DDL/DML/query/ops statements, see Chapter 4 Secondary indexes Backfill on creation, automatic maintenance on DML, query optimization for equality/range scans and ORDER BY Replication master-follower async replication (M2), with async / semi-sync / sync modes (T33) Sharding Logical sharding: RegionInfo metadata + Router half-open [StartKey, EndKey) + region-prefixed physical keys (M3) Multi-node cluster Node topology, cluster route table (region → node), cross-node SELECT forwarding & merge (M4) Distributed write / 2PC Cross-node write atomicity via two-phase commit (M5) HA / Failover Heartbeat-based failure detection, automatic region re-assignment, read failover, replication master failover (M6) Region split & load balancing Write-path auto-split, manual/periodic load balancing, online migration (M7) Distributed transactions / TSO Global monotonic timestamp, distributed snapshot isolation, 2PC recovery hardening (M8) Backup & Restore (BR) Consistent-snapshot logical backup, idempotent restore, LSN-based PITR Client drivers JDBC & Python drivers (T19) wrapping the pkg/server protocol Ops toolchain openxdb doctor / stats , one-click deploy scripts (T20) Security TLS transport encryption (T36), RBAC roles & privileges (M11/M17), audit log (T30) Observability Slow query log, Prometheus metrics, status view, alert rules (M13/T37) Ecosystem interop CSV/JSON Lines/Parquet export (M19), mysqldump-compatible import (M14) 1.3 Architecture Layers ¶ Layer Package Responsibility Protocol + CLI cmd/openxdb , pkg/server TCP server, REPL, binary protocol framing SQL pkg/sql Recursive-descent parser, executor (project/filter/sort/aggregate), metadata catalog, secondary index layer Transaction pkg/txn Begin/commit/rollback, snapshot isolation, read-your-writes Storage pkg/storage KV interface, key encoding; RocksDB engine and B+Tree engine WAL pkg/wal Append-only log, replay recovery Replication pkg/replication , pkg/txn , pkg/db Binlog store, master replicator (push + heartbeat), follower idempotent apply, commit-hook wiring Sharding pkg/sharding , pkg/sql , pkg/db RegionInfo metadata, Router key→region mapping, region-prefixed physical keys, cross-region query merge, split management Cluster pkg/cluster , pkg/sql , pkg/db Node registry (m:nodes), handshake/liveness, cluster route table (region→node), cross-node SELECT forwarding + merge, region data load (REGION_PUSH) Distributed write / 2PC pkg/cluster , pkg/sql/2pc.go , pkg/db Two-phase commit coordinator, participant prepare persistence, idempotent commit/abort, crash recovery HA / Failover pkg/cluster , pkg/sql/ha.go , pkg/db/ha.go Heartbeat timeout → node down, automatic region re-assignment, read failover, replication master failover Split & Balance pkg/sql/balance.go , pkg/cluster , pkg/db Write-path auto-split, manual/auto load balancing, cluster-not-enabled guard Global Timestamp (TSO) pkg/tso , pkg/cluster/tso.go , pkg/db Global monotonic timestamp (64-bit ms + logical layout), batch issuance, overflow protection, transaction-boundary Reset Snapshot Isolation (distributed) pkg/cluster/txn2pc.go , pkg/sql/executor.go , pkg/db Version records (m:ver), begin_ts/commit_ts global filtering, cross-node version passthrough Backup / Restore pkg/sql/backup.go , pkg/sql , pkg/db Consistent-snapshot logical backup (single file, version + CRC32), idempotent restore, binlog replay to target LSN Data dir pkg/db Initialization, engine + WAL + txn manager wiring, crash recovery 1.4 Key Encoding ¶ physical key: r{regionID:8B}{innerKey} row key: s{tableID:8B}{pk} (inner, M1) index key: i{tableID:8B}{indexID:8B}{idxVal}p{pk} (inner, T6) Every stored key carries a region prefix ( r + 8-byte big-endian regionID); the inner key keeps the M1/T6 layout, so keys stay contiguous within a region and region boundaries are explicit. Index values use sort-friendly encoding: INT flips the sign bit ( v ^ 0x8000000000000000 ), TEXT stays raw bytes, so byte order equals value order. 2. Quick Start ¶ 2.1 Build Requirements ¶ Go 1.22+ A C/C++ toolchain for cgo (e.g., MinGW-w64 on Windows, gcc/clang on Linux/macOS) RocksDB (tested with v11.8.1 source build, no third-party compression libs) 2.2 Build (Windows + MinGW + Go) ¶ One-shot reproducible build scripts (auto-detect RocksDB install, then go build + optional go test ): # Windows: build bin\openxdb.exe, verify go build ./..., run go test ./... powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1 -RunTests # explicit paths: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1 -RocksSrcDir C:\rocksdb-src -RocksBuildDir C:\rocksdb-build -RunTests # Linux/macOS: ./scripts/build.sh --test ./scripts/build.sh --rocks-src /path/to/rocksdb-11.8.1 --rocks-build /path/to/librocksdb-dir --test Manual cgo setup (equivalent, for custom toolchains): export CGO_CFLAGS=-I<rocksdb>/include export CGO_CXXFLAGS=-I<rocksdb>/include export CGO_LDFLAGS=-L<rocksdb-build> -lrocksdb # Windows: add -lshlwapi -lrpcrt4 -lws2_32 go build ./... pkg/storage/rocksdb declares per-platform #cgo link flags (Windows -lwinpthread -lshlwapi -lrpcrt4 -lws2_32 , Linux -lstdc++ -lpthread , Darwin -lstdc++ ), so only the RocksDB include/lib dirs need to be supplied via CGO_CFLAGS / CGO_LDFLAGS . Note : the repository #cgo flags include -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc ; do not add undeclared link flags such as -lstdc++ / -lz , which can cause link conflicts. 2.3 Start REPL / TCP Server ¶ # initialize a data directory openxdb init --data-dir ./data # local REPL openxdb repl --data-dir ./data # TCP server (default port 7788) openxdb start --data-dir ./data [--port 7788] # ops: health check + live metrics openxdb doctor --data-dir ./data [--addr 127.0.0.1:7788] [--json] openxdb stats [--addr 127.0.0.1:7788] [--interval 5] [--json] 2.4 Create Table, Insert, Query Example ¶ CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name TEXT, age INT, PRIMARY KEY (id)); INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'alice', 30), (2, 'bob', 25), (3, 'carol', 35); CREATE INDEX idx_age ON users (age); SELECT name FROM users WHERE age >= 25 AND age < 35 ORDER BY age; UPDATE users SET age = 31 WHERE id = 1; DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 3; 2.5 Run Tests ¶ go test ./... All packages pass: cluster (node handshake, query forwarding, heartbeat down, region push route learning, idempotent node re-register), db (replication integration, M4 two-node integration, M5 2PC integration, M6 HA integration, M7 split/balance integration, M8 distributed-txn integration, BR backup/restore integration), replication , server , sharding , sql , storage , storage/btree , storage/rocksdb , tso , txn , wal . 3. Installation & Deployment ¶ 3.1 Configuration File openxdb.conf ¶ OpenXDB uses an INI-style configuration file (see docs/openxdb.conf.example ). Core sections: [server] data_dir = ./data port = 7788 replica_port = 7789 metrics_port = 7790 # tls_cert = cert.pem # tls_key = key.pem [sql] query_cache = on slow_query_threshold = 100 backup_dir = ./backup [server] : data_dir data directory, port main service port (default 7788), replica_port replication port, metrics_port Prometheus metrics port, tls_cert / tls_key TLS certificate and private key paths. [sql] : query_cache query cache switch, slow_query_threshold slow query threshold in milliseconds (default 100ms), backup_dir backup directory. Start with a config file: openxdb start --config openxdb.conf Tip: hot-reloadable items (e.g., query_cache , slow_query_threshold , slow_query_log ) can also be changed at runtime via SET / SET PERSIST — see ops statements in Chapter 4 . 3.2 One-Click Deploy Scripts ¶ The repository ships Windows and Linux/macOS deploy scripts: # Windows powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\deploy.ps1 -DataDir C:\openxdb\data -Port 7788 # Linux/macOS ./scripts/deploy.sh --data-dir /var/lib/openxdb --port 7788 Script flow: parameterized init ( -DataDir / -Port / --data-dir / --port ) → start → openxdb doctor health self-check → deployment summary. 3.3 Startup Modes ¶ Command Description openxdb init --data-dir <dir> Initialize a data directory openxdb repl --data-dir <dir> Local interactive REPL openxdb start --data-dir <dir> [--port 7788] Start TCP server (default port 7788) openxdb start --cluster-addr <addr> Start in cluster mode (node ID via --node-id or auto-generated) openxdb doctor Health check (exit codes 0=pass / 1=warn / 2=error) openxdb stats Live metrics openxdb gen-cert cert.pem key.pem Generate self-signed TLS certificate 4. SQL Reference ¶ All syntax in this chapter comes from README.md and T* design documents under docs/. The SQL capability list includes T41/T42 additions (IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, INSERT INTO SELECT). 4.1 Data Types ¶ Type Description INT Integer TEXT Text DATE Date DECIMAL Fixed-point decimal (normalized to fixed 4 decimal places internally) BLOB Binary large object 4.2 DDL ¶ CREATE TABLE ¶ -- Basic create (inline PRIMARY KEY is equivalent to table-level PRIMARY KEY) CREATE TABLE users ( id INT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, age INT ); CREATE TABLE orders ( id INT, user_id INT, amount DECIMAL, PRIMARY KEY (id) ); -- IF NOT EXISTS: idempotent create (T41) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); -- CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS, T41): create a table from query results CREATE TABLE adult_users AS SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE age >= 18; CREATE INDEX ¶ CREATE INDEX idx_age ON users (age); Views / Materialized Views / Triggers / Stored Procedures ¶ -- View CREATE VIEW v_adult AS SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE age >= 18; DROP VIEW v_adult; -- Materialized view CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_adult AS SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE age >= 18; REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_adult; DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_adult; -- Trigger CREATE TRIGGER trg_after_insert AFTER INSERT ON users FOR EACH ROW ...; DROP TRIGGER trg_after_insert; SHOW TRIGGERS; -- Stored procedure CREATE PROCEDURE p_get_user(IN uid INT) ...; CALL p_get_user(1); DROP PROCEDURE p_get_user; SHOW PROCEDURES; Users / Roles ¶ CREATE USER 'alice' IDENTIFIED BY 'pwd123'; -- duplicate name errors DROP USER [IF EXISTS] 'alice'; -- missing errors; IF EXISTS silent SHOW USERS; -- sorted by name ALTER USER 'alice' IDENTIFIED BY 'newpwd'; -- reset password CREATE ROLE 'analyst'; DROP ROLE [IF EXISTS] 'analyst'; SHOW ROLES; GRANT ROLE 'analyst' TO 'alice'; REVOKE ROLE 'analyst' FROM 'alice'; SHOW GRANTS FOR 'alice'; DROP ... IF EXISTS ¶ DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS : idempotent when the table is missing (T21 fix). DROP USER IF EXISTS / DROP ROLE IF EXISTS : idempotent. Dropping users/tables/roles cascades cleanup of related grants. 4.3 DML ¶ INSERT ¶ INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'alice', 30), (2, 'bob', 25); INSERT INTO users (id, name) VALUES (3, 'carol'); INSERT INTO ... SELECT (T42) ¶ -- Insert query results into a target table (column list optional; full SELECT source compatibility; atomic transaction + rollback) INSERT INTO archive_users SELECT * FROM users WHERE age >= 30; INSERT INTO archive_users (id, name) SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE age >= 30; Self-insert uses snapshot semantics (self-insert snapshot semantics). REPLACE INTO ... SELECT is also supported. REPLACE / UPSERT ¶ -- REPLACE: on primary-key conflict, delete then insert REPLACE INTO users VALUES (1, 'alice2', 31); -- INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE: update on conflict INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'alice', 30) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE age = 31; UPDATE / DELETE ¶ UPDATE users SET age = 31 WHERE id = 1; DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 3; 4.4 Query (Full SELECT Capabilities) ¶ -- Basic query + WHERE SELECT * FROM users WHERE age >= 25; -- ORDER BY & pagination (LIMIT/OFFSET also works on GROUP BY/aggregate results, T40) SELECT name FROM users ORDER BY age LIMIT 10 OFFSET 5; -- GROUP BY + aggregates (MAX/MIN/COUNT/SUM/AVG; MAX/MIN added in T40) SELECT age, COUNT(*), SUM(amount), AVG(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY age; SELECT MAX(age), MIN(age) FROM users; -- DISTINCT (T40) SELECT DISTINCT age FROM users; -- JOIN SELECT u.name, o.amount FROM users u JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id; -- Subquery SELECT name FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders WHERE amount > 100); -- CTE (M10) WITH adult AS (SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE age >= 18) SELECT * FROM adult; -- Window functions (M10) SELECT name, age, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY age) AS rn FROM users; -- BETWEEN / IN / LIKE SELECT * FROM users WHERE age BETWEEN 25 AND 35; SELECT * FROM users WHERE name IN ('alice', 'bob'); SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE 'a%'; -- CASE WHEN & expressions (arithmetic expressions added in T40) SELECT name, CASE WHEN age >= 18 THEN 'adult' ELSE 'minor' END AS bucket FROM users; SELECT id, amount * 2 AS double_amount FROM orders; SELECT -age AS neg_age FROM users; 4.5 Transactions ¶ BEGIN; INSERT INTO users VALUES (4, 'dave', 40); UPDATE users SET age = 41 WHERE id = 4; COMMIT; -- or roll back BEGIN; DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 4; ROLLBACK; Transaction characteristics: local ACID + snapshot isolation; read-your-writes merge, tombstones, point/range scan. 4.6 Data Import / Export ¶ -- CSV import (P1) IMPORT INTO users FROM '/path/users.csv'; -- mysqldump-compatible import (M14, T27): parses mysqldump CREATE TABLE + INSERT statements IMPORT MYSQLDUMP FROM '/path/dump.sql' [BATCH 100] [IGNORE ERRORS]; -- Export (P1 + M19 ecosystem export) EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.csv'; -- equivalent to FORMAT CSV EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.csv' FORMAT CSV; EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.jsonl' FORMAT JSON; -- JSON Lines EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.parquet' FORMAT PARQUET; -- Parquet v1 CSV: for spreadsheet tools. JSON (JSON Lines): streaming object sequence, one record per line, suitable for log pipelines / data-lake ingestion / ETL. Parquet: columnar binary storage produced by a self-contained minimal Parquet v1 writer (single Row Group, PLAIN/UNCOMPRESSED encoding), directly consumable by Spark/Hive/DuckDB/Polars. 4.7 Ops Statements ¶ SHOW Statements ¶ SHOW TABLES; -- list all tables SHOW INDEX FROM users; -- show indexes of a table SHOW VIEWS; -- list views SHOW USERS; -- list users SHOW ROLES; -- list roles SHOW GRANTS FOR 'alice'; -- show grants of a user SHOW TRIGGERS; -- list triggers SHOW PROCEDURES; -- list stored procedures SHOW SLOWQUERIES; -- slow queries (newest first; columns: time|user|duration_ms|rows|error|sql) SHOW STATS; -- service status metrics SHOW CONFIG; -- show current configuration SHOW PERSISTED CONFIG; -- show persisted configuration SHOW AUDITLOG; -- audit log SHOW ALERT RULES; -- alert rules SHOW ALERT STATUS; -- alert status SHOW ALERTS; -- alert events SHOW NODES; -- cluster nodes SHOW REGION ROUTES; -- region routes (region/table/start/end/node/local) LIST REGIONS; -- list regions LOCATE REGION <key>; -- locate the region containing a key EXPLAIN ¶ EXPLAIN <SELECT>; SET / SET PERSIST ¶ SET slow_query_threshold = 100; -- slow query threshold (ms; <=0 disables recording) SET slow_query_log = on; -- slow query file logging switch SET query_cache = on; -- query cache switch SET replication_mode = async; -- replication mode: async / semi-sync / sync SET replication_ack = 1; -- semi-sync ACK count SET replication_timeout = 3000; -- ACK timeout (ms) SET alert_rules = '...'; -- alert rules (JSON) SET audit_log = on; -- audit log hot switch SET PERSIST slow_query_threshold = 100; -- persist configuration (restart-effective class) SET PERSIST tls_cert = 'cert.pem'; -- TLS certificate (restart-effective) SET PERSIST tls_key = 'key.pem'; -- TLS private key (restart-effective) SET PERSIST tls_allow_legacy = on; -- allow plaintext/TLS coexistence listener SET @var = 1; -- user variable SELECT @var; -- read user variable BACKUP / RESTORE ¶ BACKUP TO '/path/backup.bk'; -- consistent-snapshot logical backup RESTORE FROM '/path/backup.bk'; -- idempotent restore (same-named tables drop-then-recreate) RESTORE FROM '/path/backup.bk' TO LSN 12345; -- PITR: replay binlog after backup point up to target LSN PREPARE / EXECUTE / DEALLOCATE (M18) ¶ PREPARE stmt1 FROM 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?'; EXECUTE stmt1 USING 1; -- bind user variables or literals EXECUTE stmt1 USING @var; DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt1; Session-scoped cache: re-PREPARE of the same name overwrites; EXECUTE/DEALLOCATE of unknown names errors; argument count must match placeholder count. information_schema Read-Only Views (M18) ¶ SELECT * FROM information_schema.schemata; SELECT * FROM information_schema.tables; SELECT * FROM information_schema.columns; SELECT * FROM information_schema.statistics; Read-only virtual database: case-insensitive column projection, WHERE <col> = <literal> equality filters (AND-combinable), ORDER BY, qualified default.information_schema.tables FROM; any CREATE/DROP/INSERT/UPDATE targeting the virtual library is rejected. 5. Client Drivers ¶ OpenXDB ships JDBC and Python standard client drivers (T19), both based on the self-developed binary TCP protocol ( pkg/server ) — not MySQL wire protocol . 5.1 Protocol Notes ¶ Wire protocol: UTF-8 line protocol; each command is one line ending with \n ; the server replies line by line. Reply forms: simple confirmation (OK/PONG/BYE), affected rows (N rows affected), text table (header row + separator + data rows + trailing N rows), error (ERR ). Empty cells map uniformly to NULL. Multi-line text is unsupported ( \n / \r in parameterized string values are rejected by the driver). Parameterization: the server protocol has no prepared-statement binary parameter channel; both drivers safely escape ? placeholders client-side. 5.2 JDBC Driver ¶ Location: drivers/jdbc , Maven project, Java 8+, JUnit 5. Registration: static block DriverManager.registerDriver(new OpenXDBDriver()) + META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver auto-registration. URL: jdbc:openxdb://host:port (default port 7788); user / password properties are accepted but ignored by default (runs as root when no AUTH handshake is exchanged). Core classes: OpenXDBDriver / OpenXDBConnection / OpenXDBStatement / OpenXDBPreparedStatement (client-side ? placeholder substitution) / OpenXDBResultSet (forward-only, read-only) / OpenXDBProtocol (socket connection with 5s timeout). Transactions: setAutoCommit(false) triggers a session transaction; sends BEGIN automatically if not started before execution. TLS: the driver supports TLS connections ( InsecureTLSConfig can disable certificate verification for dev; use verify-full / verify-ca in production). 5.3 Python Driver ¶ Location: drivers/python , PEP 249 compliant. Metadata: apilevel="2.0" , threadsafety=1 , paramstyle="qmark" , __version__="0.10.0" . Module-level connect() , DEFAULT_PORT ; PEP 249 style error hierarchy. import openxdb conn = openxdb.connect("127.0.0.1", 7788) cur = conn.cursor() cur.execute("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?", (1,)) for row in cur.fetchall(): print(row) conn.close() Connection : cursor() / ping() / begin() / commit() / rollback() / close() . Cursor : execute / executemany / fetchone / fetchmany / fetchall / iterator. TLS: the driver supports TLS connection parameters (disable certificate verification for self-signed dev certs; use a trusted CA in production). 6. Data Security ¶ 6.1 Backup & Restore (BR) ¶ Consistent-snapshot logical backup : BACKUP TO <path> snapshots the full table catalog, all data rows, index keys, and region routing metadata on a single consistent snapshot, plus the backup-point LSN. Produces a single transportable file (magic + version + JSON meta + per-segment CRC32 integrity checks + atomic tmp+rename write). Idempotent restore : RESTORE FROM <path> validates version/integrity first, then rebuilds tables/data/indexes/routing with "drop-then-recreate" semantics for same-named tables (stale rows/index residue cleared, catalog overwritten, whole restore runs in one transaction with full rollback). PITR (point-in-time recovery) : RESTORE FROM <path> TO LSN <n> replays binlog records after the backup point up to the target LSN (inclusive) — the backup + binlog-replay PITR foundation. Distributed backup consistency (T35) : a coordinator initiates multi-node consistent backup: PREPARE collects per-node LastLSN/TSO candidates → GlobalLSN = max(all LSN) as the global consistency point → DO phase snapshots each node with the aligned global_lsn (retry up to 3 rounds if a node exceeds G); artifacts keep v1 format + a manifest (GlobalLSN / node metadata / consistency marker); RESTORE ... TO LSN G drives every node to the global backup point; single-node zero-trigger keeps legacy BACKUP/RESTORE intact. 6.2 TLS Transport Encryption (T36) ¶ The main service listener supports TLS: when --tls-cert and --tls-key are both provided, encrypted listening is enabled; otherwise plaintext (behavior-compatible). The replica port ( --replica-port ) can be separately enabled with --replica-tls . TLS-only listener by default , plaintext rejected; --tls-allow-legacy or SET PERSIST tls_allow_legacy=on enables plaintext/TLS coexistence (AutoListener). Certificate management: openxdb gen-cert cert.pem key.pem generates a self-signed certificate (dev/test only; use a trusted-CA-signed certificate in production and never commit private keys); SET PERSIST tls_cert/tls_key are restart-effective configs. Client verification: drivers support verify-full / verify-ca ; disable verification for self-signed dev certs. # Generate a self-signed certificate (openssl method) openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -subj "/CN=openxdb" # Start TLS service (both flags required; providing only one errors out) openxdb start --data-dir ./data --tls-cert cert.pem --tls-key key.pem # Verify TLS handshake openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:7788 -CAfile cert.pem 6.3 RBAC & Privileges ¶ User management : CREATE USER / DROP USER [IF EXISTS] / ALTER USER / SHOW USERS ; passwords are stored as SHA-256 + per-user random salt hashes (no plaintext), with constant-time comparison against timing side channels. Table-level privileges : GRANT <priv[,priv...]> ON <table> TO '<user>' / REVOKE ... FROM '<user>' ; priv ∈ {SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, ALL}; repeated GRANT/REVOKE are idempotent. Database-level & column-level privileges (M17) : GRANT/REVOKE <priv> ON DATABASE <db> TO/FROM '<user>' , GRANT/REVOKE <priv> ON <table> (<col>, ...) TO/FROM ... ; role-targeted grants. Role system (M17) : CREATE ROLE / DROP ROLE [IF EXISTS] / SHOW ROLES , GRANT ROLE '<role>' TO '<user>' / REVOKE ROLE ... FROM '<user>' , SHOW GRANTS FOR '<user>' . Aggregated privilege checks : table direct ∪ database ∪ role inheritance for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, plus column-level checks. Cascade cleanup : DROP USER / DROP TABLE / DROP ROLE automatically clean related grants to avoid dangling authorizations. Connection auth : the server supports optional connection auth (AUTH handshake); without it the connection runs as the default root user; when AllowLegacy is enabled legacy clients fall back to a restricted guest mode, or are rejected in strict mode. 6.4 Audit Log (T30) ¶ Audited events: connect, auth, DML, DDL, privilege events. Storage: ring buffer + JSON Lines persistence. Query: SHOW AUDITLOG ; hot switch: SET audit_log = on/off . 7. Operations & Observability ¶ 7.1 openxdb doctor Health Check (T20) ¶ openxdb doctor --data-dir ./data [--addr 127.0.0.1:7788] [--json] Checks: - Data directory & WAL integrity; - RocksDB open health; - m:tables / m:regions metadata consistency & route self-consistency; - Binlog readability & LSN (read-only PeekLastLSN ); - Optional online port/PING and slow-query checks. Output: human-readable or --json report; exit codes 0=pass / 1=warn / 2=error. 7.2 openxdb stats Live Metrics (T20) ¶ openxdb stats [--addr 127.0.0.1:7788] [--interval 5] [--json] Metrics: active connections (server session counter), table count, region count & route distribution, slow query count, binlog LSN (optional two-sample growth via --interval ), table or --json output; backed by the SHOW STATS statement. 7.3 Prometheus Metrics (M13) ¶ Metrics port: metrics_port (default 7790), exposing Prometheus-format metrics. Metrics source: same metrics.Snapshot data source (connections, table/region counts, slow queries, LSN, etc.). 7.4 Slow Queries (M13) ¶ Threshold: default 100ms; SET slow_query_threshold = <ms> (<=0 disables recording). File logging: default <data_dir>/slow.log , configurable; SET slow_query_log = on/off hot switch. In-memory: keeps the most recent N records (default 64, adjustable via Engine.SetSlowQueryMax(n) ); query via SHOW SLOWQUERIES (newest first). Record fields: SQL text, user, start time, duration (ms), result rows (0 on failure), error message (empty on success). Low-overhead design: threshold check before formatting; normal statements incur zero formatting cost. 7.5 Alert Rules (T37) ¶ Rule model: metric / op / threshold / duration_sec / severity , stored as JSON. Configuration: SET / SET PERSIST alert_rules* . Evaluation engine: over the same metrics.Snapshot data source, NORMAL/ALERT/RESOLVED state machine + duration debounce. Notification: logx ring buffer + optional webhook / file channel. Management statements: SHOW ALERT RULES / SHOW ALERT STATUS / SHOW ALERTS . Evaluation loop wired to the database lifecycle. 7.6 Region Split & Load Balancing (M7) ¶ Auto-split : the write path (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) accumulates per-table write counters after commits; at half the row threshold a real row-count check runs (scans the local region's physical key space); a local region exceeding the threshold is split in half along its data midpoint inside the same transaction (existing rows re-routed, route table replaced, metadata persisted). Manual split : SPLIT REGION (by data midpoint) or explicit boundaries. Manual balance : BALANCE (returns number of migrated regions; a second BALANCE returns 0). Auto balance : Engine.SetAutoBalance(enabled, interval) periodic trigger; compares local region counts with the least-loaded live node and migrates the largest region there. Online migration : source route unchanged during migration, reads/writes uninterrupted; scan source region rows → REGION_PUSH loads the target → switch local route and persist; other live nodes learn the new owner via the next heartbeat route sync. Single-node mode BALANCE reports cluster not enabled . 7.7 HA Failover (M6) ¶ Failure detection : heartbeat (PING/PONG, default 2s/6s) timeout → node marked down (OnDown callback). Automatic region re-assignment : regions owned by the down node are re-assigned to a live node (fullest replica scan + REGION_PUSH ), replacing manual ASSIGN REGION . Read failover : cross-node reads transparently re-route to the new owner (QUERY_REQ re-routed), no client error. Replication master failover : follower auto-promotes when the old master is down ( PromoteToMaster / EnableAutoFailover / StopAutoFailover ), keeping the write path available. 8. Distributed Capabilities ¶ 8.1 Replication (M2 + T33) ¶ Async replication (default) : master-follower; commit-hook binlog (independent append-only file, monotonically increasing LSN); replicator push with per-slot resume; follower idempotent apply; PING/PONG heartbeats with offline detection. Semi-sync replication : SET replication_mode = semi-sync ; waits for partial/full ACK (outside the transaction lock); degrades to async on ACK timeout or no slave. Sync replication : SET replication_mode = sync ; waits for all ACKs; refuses pseudo-sync when requirements cannot be met. Hot-switch config: SET replication_mode / SET replication_ack / SET replication_timeout . 8.2 Sharding (M3) ¶ RegionInfo metadata persisted as m:regions ; Router with half-open [StartKey, EndKey) boundary semantics. Region-prefixed physical keys ( r + regionID:8B + inner key). Cross-region point/range/full-table queries via range expansion + merge. Management: SPLIT / LIST REGIONS / LOCATE REGION ; default single-region shape keeps pre-sharding behavior unchanged. 8.3 Multi-Node Cluster (M4) ¶ Node topology: NodeInfo (NodeID/Addr/Role master|follower/State active|down + last seen), node registry persisted to m:nodes , auto-restored on open. Management: ADD NODE '<addr>' / SHOW NODES ; openxdb start --cluster-addr <addr> starts cluster mode. Cluster route table: region → node; ASSIGN REGION <id> TO NODE '<nodeID>' updates ownership and pushes data; SHOW REGION ROUTES shows everything in one table. Cross-node reads: non-local regions are forwarded over TCP to their owning node and merged back; Local semantics (Node empty or equal to selfID) keep single-node deployments at zero regression. 8.4 Distributed Write / 2PC (M5) ¶ Cross-node write atomicity: autocommit INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (incl. CSV IMPORT) touching both local and remote regions execute as two-phase commit. Flow: coordinator applies local ops → PREPAREs remote participants (ops persisted under m:2pc:* for crash recovery) → commits locally → idempotently COMMITs all participants. Failure semantics: any PREPARE failure or local commit failure ABORTs the whole statement; error codes TXN_PREPARE_FAILED / TXN_COMMIT_ABORTED / TXN_COMMIT_UNCERTAIN . Protocol frames 22-27 extend M4 framing; single-node deployments never enter the 2PC path (zero regression). 8.5 Distributed Transactions / TSO (M8) ¶ Global Timestamp (TSO) : 64-bit physical-ms + 24-bit logical layout; strict monotonicity (clock-fallback safe); batch issuance (GetBatch allocates contiguous ranges, remote clients cache a batch to amortize RTT); transaction-boundary Reset drops unconsumed cache so a new snapshot reads from the authoritative sequence head. Distributed snapshot isolation : version records m:ver:<key>:<commit_ts> (key-first so per-key ranges stay contiguous); begin_ts/commit_ts globally comparable across nodes with cross-node passthrough. 2PC recovery hardening : coordinator persists CoordRecord ( m:2pc:coord:<txid> ), decides commit/abort on restart (RecoverCoordinated2PC), and idempotently drives participants to completion ( TXN_COMMIT_UNCERTAIN completion). 8.6 Cross-Node DDL (T34) ¶ DDL metadata is broadcast to all online nodes via cluster DDL_PUSH frames; each node applies idempotently by TableID. Offline/apply-failure nodes record pending items, replayed before the next broadcast or via ReplayPendingDDL . Single-node zero-trigger compatibility; works alongside the T33 replication chain. 8.7 Distributed Backup Consistency (T35) ¶ See section 6.1 . 9. Performance Benchmark ¶ Source: E5 standard bench alignment experiment ( docs/experiments/E5_standard_bench_alignment.md ). Because OpenXDB speaks a self-developed protocol (not MySQL wire protocol), standard sysbench/TPC-C official tools cannot connect directly; we used Python PEP 249 driver equivalence with real measurements. Performance positioning is single-node edge benchmark . 9.1 sysbench OLTP (8 threads × 60s, Python driver, self-developed protocol) ¶ Workload TPS QPS errs read (read-only) 1.73 24.27 0 write (write-only) 0.93 3.73 0 read_write (mixed) 1.32 23.70 0 9.2 TPC-C Small Warehouse (5 warehouses × 8 threads × 120s) ¶ Metric Value errs tpmC 13.50 0 TPM 32.50 0 9.3 Bottleneck Notes ¶ Current throughput bottleneck: global session-lock serialization + per-statement round trips (each statement is exchanged between driver and server one by one). E5 also fixed a shared-session concurrency bug and completed arithmetic-expression / DISTINCT / DECIMAL-precision workarounds. Historical benchmark references: E3 SQL OLTP end-to-end 256.3 TPS (8:2) / 605.4 TPS (5:5); E4 stability 6-min mixed load 307–385 TPS without degradation, restart COUNT(*) == 150466; E2 fsync engine benchmark sync write 747k TPS seq / 198k rand (batch=1000), group-commit batch 181x vs per-key fsync. These are experiment records, not external commitments. 10. Known Limitations & Boundaries ¶ For the full list see KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md (to be created). Summary: SQL subset : OpenXDB implements a SQL subset, not the full SQL standard. The HAVING clause is not supported; DDL/DML/query capabilities are as defined in Chapter 4 . Not MySQL wire protocol : uses a self-developed binary TCP protocol, so MySQL ecosystem tools (standard sysbench, official mysqldump client, etc.) cannot directly connect. Global session-lock performance boundary : the current serialized global session lock is the primary throughput bottleneck (see Chapter 9 ); high-concurrency write throughput is limited. Line protocol limits : cell newlines are unsupported (multi-line parameter strings are rejected by drivers); empty cells represent both NULL and empty string. Types & precision : DECIMAL is normalized to fixed 4 decimal places internally; in JSON export DECIMAL is approximated via strconv.ParseFloat (or kept as a string). Auth & legacy mode : without an AUTH handshake connections run as the default root user; legacy clients fall back to a restricted guest mode when AllowLegacy is enabled, or are rejected in strict mode. Stored procedures/triggers are a restricted subset : only the syntax and semantics defined in the design documents are supported; no full SQL/PL capabilities. Distributed statements limited in single-node mode : BALANCE and similar cluster statements explicitly report cluster not enabled ; cross-node writes require cluster mode. Distributed capability boundaries : cross-node writes rely on 2PC protocol frames; replication modes (async/semi-sync/sync) are switched via hot config; sync mode refuses pseudo-sync when ACKs cannot be satisfied. Import compatibility : mysqldump import is text-rule parsing covering a common dump syntax subset; unknown types error in strict mode and skip the table in lenient mode; cell parse failures drop the row in lenient mode. 11. FAQ ¶ Q1: cgo link errors during build? ¶ Check that the CGO environment variables point to RocksDB: CGO_CFLAGS / CGO_CXXFLAGS → <rocksdb>/include , CGO_LDFLAGS → <rocksdb-build> -lrocksdb . On Windows add -lshlwapi -lrpcrt4 -lws2_32 (already in repository #cgo ). Prefer scripts/build.ps1 / scripts/build.sh for one-shot builds. Do not add undeclared flags such as -lstdc++ / -lz . Q2: Table names colliding with keywords (e.g., users vs SHOW USERS )? ¶ SHOW USERS is implemented by identifier text matching; USERS is not in the keyword table, so CREATE TABLE users and SHOW USERS coexist without special handling. For other keyword conflicts, consult the parsing rules in the design documents. Q3: What is the idempotency semantics of IF NOT EXISTS? ¶ CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / DROP TABLE IF EXISTS / DROP USER IF EXISTS / DROP ROLE IF EXISTS succeed silently when the object does not exist; when it exists, normal semantics apply (create errors or drop succeeds). Q4: How to back up and restore? ¶ BACKUP TO '<path>' produces a single-file consistent-snapshot backup; RESTORE FROM '<path>' idempotently restores (same-named tables drop-then-recreate); for point-in-time recovery use RESTORE FROM '<path>' TO LSN <n> to replay binlog up to the target LSN. For distributed clusters use the T35 coordinator for multi-node consistent backup. Q5: How to set up a cluster? ¶ Initialize each node with openxdb init --data-dir <dir> , then start in cluster mode with openxdb start --cluster-addr <addr> ; register peers with ADD NODE '<addr>' , assign region ownership with ASSIGN REGION <id> TO NODE '<nodeID>' , and inspect with SHOW NODES / SHOW REGION ROUTES . Q6: How do drivers connect? ¶ JDBC: jdbc:openxdb://host:7788 ; Python: openxdb.connect("host", 7788) . Both drivers use the self-developed protocol with ? placeholders (client-side safe escaping). For TLS, configure certificate verification mode in JDBC and pass TLS connection parameters in Python. Q7: Why can't I connect with the MySQL client? ¶ OpenXDB uses a self-developed binary TCP protocol ( pkg/server ), not MySQL wire protocol, so the official MySQL client cannot connect directly. Use the built-in REPL ( openxdb repl ) or the JDBC / Python drivers. Q8: How do I view slow queries? ¶ SET slow_query_threshold = <ms> sets the threshold (default 100ms); after executing statements, SHOW SLOWQUERIES shows recent records; SET slow_query_log = on enables file logging (default <data_dir>/slow.log ). Q9: How do I enable TLS? ¶ Generate a certificate, then start with openxdb start --data-dir ./data --tls-cert cert.pem --tls-key key.pem (both flags required); TLS-only is the default with plaintext rejected; SET PERSIST tls_allow_legacy=on enables plaintext/TLS coexistence. Use --replica-tls for the replica port. Q10: Are the performance numbers trustworthy? Why is TPS low? ¶ All performance numbers come from the E5 standard bench alignment experiment ( docs/experiments/E5_standard_bench_alignment.md ) with real measurements (8 threads × 60s / 120s, 0 errors). The current throughput bottleneck is global session-lock serialization + per-statement round trips; the project positions itself as a single-node edge benchmark — functional completeness first, performance optimization ongoing. This manual is compiled from the OpenXDB README.md and docs/ design documents, v1.0.0.

docs.text: OpenXDB is a from-scratch single-node/distributed relational database kernel written in Go, with a storage engine built on top of RocksDB (accessed through a thin cgo bridge). The kernel fully includes WAL (write-ahead log), transactions, SQL parsing & execution, replication, sharding, 2PC, HA (high availability), backup & restore — evolving from a learning/experimentation kernel into one with complete distributed capabilities.
docs.title: 1. Product Overview & Positioning

docs.text: OpenXDB speaks a self-developed binary TCP protocol ( pkg/server ) and is not a MySQL wire protocol implementation. It therefore cannot directly interoperate with MySQL ecosystem tools (e.g., standard sysbench, mysqldump beyond the built-in import, binlog tools). Performance positioning is single-node edge benchmark : the kernel implements the full functional chain, and performance optimization is still ongoing; measured throughput is presented in Chapter 9 . OpenXDB does not position itself against TiDB, TDSQL, or MySQL. It is an independently implemented kernel for learning, experimentation, and edge scenarios.
docs.title: 1.1 Positioning Boundaries

docs.title: 1.3 Architecture Layers

docs.text: physical key: r{regionID:8B}{innerKey} row key: s{tableID:8B}{pk} (inner, M1) index key: i{tableID:8B}{indexID:8B}{idxVal}p{pk} (inner, T6) Every stored key carries a region prefix ( r + 8-byte big-endian regionID); the inner key keeps the M1/T6 layout, so keys stay contiguous within a region and region boundaries are explicit. Index values use sort-friendly encoding: INT flips the sign bit ( v ^ 0x8000000000000000 ), TEXT stays raw bytes, so byte order equals value order.

docs.text: One-shot reproducible build scripts (auto-detect RocksDB install, then go build + optional go test ): # Windows: build bin\openxdb.exe, verify go build ./..., run go test ./... powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1 -RunTests # explicit paths: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build.ps1 -RocksSrcDir C:\rocksdb-src -RocksBuildDir C:\rocksdb-build -RunTests # Linux/macOS: ./scripts/build.sh --test ./scripts/build.sh --rocks-src /path/to/rocksdb-11.8.1 --rocks-build /path/to/librocksdb-dir --test Manual cgo setup (equivalent, for custom toolchains): export CGO_CFLAGS=-I<rocksdb>/include export CGO_CXXFLAGS=-I<rocksdb>/include export CGO_LDFLAGS=-L<rocksdb-build> -lrocksdb # Windows: add -lshlwapi -lrpcrt4 -lws2_32 go build ./... pkg/storage/rocksdb declares per-platform #cgo link flags (Windows -lwinpthread -lshlwapi -lrpcrt4 -lws2_32 , Linux -lstdc++ -lpthread , Darwin -lstdc++ ), so only the RocksDB include/lib dirs need to be supplied via CGO_CFLAGS / CGO_LDFLAGS . Note : the repository #cgo flags include -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc ; do not add undeclared link flags such as -lstdc++ / -lz , which can cause link conflicts.

docs.text: OpenXDB uses an INI-style configuration file (see docs/openxdb.conf.example ). Core sections: [server] data_dir = ./data port = 7788 replica_port = 7789 metrics_port = 7790 # tls_cert = cert.pem # tls_key = key.pem [sql] query_cache = on slow_query_threshold = 100 backup_dir = ./backup [server] : data_dir data directory, port main service port (default 7788), replica_port replication port, metrics_port Prometheus metrics port, tls_cert / tls_key TLS certificate and private key paths. [sql] : query_cache query cache switch, slow_query_threshold slow query threshold in milliseconds (default 100ms), backup_dir backup directory. Start with a config file: openxdb start --config openxdb.conf Tip: hot-reloadable items (e.g., query_cache , slow_query_threshold , slow_query_log ) can also be changed at runtime via SET / SET PERSIST — see ops statements in Chapter 4 .

docs.title: 4.5 Transactions

docs.text: -- CSV import (P1) IMPORT INTO users FROM '/path/users.csv'; -- mysqldump-compatible import (M14, T27): parses mysqldump CREATE TABLE + INSERT statements IMPORT MYSQLDUMP FROM '/path/dump.sql' [BATCH 100] [IGNORE ERRORS]; -- Export (P1 + M19 ecosystem export) EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.csv'; -- equivalent to FORMAT CSV EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.csv' FORMAT CSV; EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.jsonl' FORMAT JSON; -- JSON Lines EXPORT TABLE users TO '/path/users.parquet' FORMAT PARQUET; -- Parquet v1 CSV: for spreadsheet tools. JSON (JSON Lines): streaming object sequence, one record per line, suitable for log pipelines / data-lake ingestion / ETL. Parquet: columnar binary storage produced by a self-contained minimal Parquet v1 writer (single Row Group, PLAIN/UNCOMPRESSED encoding), directly consumable by Spark/Hive/DuckDB/Polars.

docs.text: OpenXDB ships JDBC and Python standard client drivers (T19), both based on the self-developed binary TCP protocol ( pkg/server ) — not MySQL wire protocol .
docs.title: 5. Client Drivers

docs.text: Wire protocol: UTF-8 line protocol; each command is one line ending with \n ; the server replies line by line. Reply forms: simple confirmation (OK/PONG/BYE), affected rows (N rows affected), text table (header row + separator + data rows + trailing N rows), error (ERR ). Empty cells map uniformly to NULL. Multi-line text is unsupported ( \n / \r in parameterized string values are rejected by the driver). Parameterization: the server protocol has no prepared-statement binary parameter channel; both drivers safely escape ? placeholders client-side.
docs.title: 5.1 Protocol Notes

docs.text: Location: drivers/jdbc , Maven project, Java 8+, JUnit 5. Registration: static block DriverManager.registerDriver(new OpenXDBDriver()) + META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver auto-registration. URL: jdbc:openxdb://host:port (default port 7788); user / password properties are accepted but ignored by default (runs as root when no AUTH handshake is exchanged). Core classes: OpenXDBDriver / OpenXDBConnection / OpenXDBStatement / OpenXDBPreparedStatement (client-side ? placeholder substitution) / OpenXDBResultSet (forward-only, read-only) / OpenXDBProtocol (socket connection with 5s timeout). Transactions: setAutoCommit(false) triggers a session transaction; sends BEGIN automatically if not started before execution. TLS: the driver supports TLS connections ( InsecureTLSConfig can disable certificate verification for dev; use verify-full / verify-ca in production).
docs.title: 5.2 JDBC Driver

docs.text: Location: drivers/python , PEP 249 compliant. Metadata: apilevel="2.0" , threadsafety=1 , paramstyle="qmark" , __version__="0.10.0" . Module-level connect() , DEFAULT_PORT ; PEP 249 style error hierarchy. import openxdb conn = openxdb.connect("127.0.0.1", 7788) cur = conn.cursor() cur.execute("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?", (1,)) for row in cur.fetchall(): print(row) conn.close() Connection : cursor() / ping() / begin() / commit() / rollback() / close() . Cursor : execute / executemany / fetchone / fetchmany / fetchall / iterator. TLS: the driver supports TLS connection parameters (disable certificate verification for self-signed dev certs; use a trusted CA in production).
docs.title: 5.3 Python Driver

docs.text: Consistent-snapshot logical backup : BACKUP TO <path> snapshots the full table catalog, all data rows, index keys, and region routing metadata on a single consistent snapshot, plus the backup-point LSN. Produces a single transportable file (magic + version + JSON meta + per-segment CRC32 integrity checks + atomic tmp+rename write). Idempotent restore : RESTORE FROM <path> validates version/integrity first, then rebuilds tables/data/indexes/routing with "drop-then-recreate" semantics for same-named tables (stale rows/index residue cleared, catalog overwritten, whole restore runs in one transaction with full rollback). PITR (point-in-time recovery) : RESTORE FROM <path> TO LSN <n> replays binlog records after the backup point up to the target LSN (inclusive) — the backup + binlog-replay PITR foundation. Distributed backup consistency (T35) : a coordinator initiates multi-node consistent backup: PREPARE collects per-node LastLSN/TSO candidates → GlobalLSN = max(all LSN) as the global consistency point → DO phase snapshots each node with the aligned global_lsn (retry up to 3 rounds if a node exceeds G); artifacts keep v1 format + a manifest (GlobalLSN / node metadata / consistency marker); RESTORE ... TO LSN G drives every node to the global backup point; single-node zero-trigger keeps legacy BACKUP/RESTORE intact.
docs.title: 6.1 Backup & Restore (BR)

docs.text: The main service listener supports TLS: when --tls-cert and --tls-key are both provided, encrypted listening is enabled; otherwise plaintext (behavior-compatible). The replica port ( --replica-port ) can be separately enabled with --replica-tls . TLS-only listener by default , plaintext rejected; --tls-allow-legacy or SET PERSIST tls_allow_legacy=on enables plaintext/TLS coexistence (AutoListener). Certificate management: openxdb gen-cert cert.pem key.pem generates a self-signed certificate (dev/test only; use a trusted-CA-signed certificate in production and never commit private keys); SET PERSIST tls_cert/tls_key are restart-effective configs. Client verification: drivers support verify-full / verify-ca ; disable verification for self-signed dev certs. # Generate a self-signed certificate (openssl method) openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -subj "/CN=openxdb" # Start TLS service (both flags required; providing only one errors out) openxdb start --data-dir ./data --tls-cert cert.pem --tls-key key.pem # Verify TLS handshake openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:7788 -CAfile cert.pem
docs.title: 6.2 TLS Transport Encryption (T36)

docs.text: User management : CREATE USER / DROP USER [IF EXISTS] / ALTER USER / SHOW USERS ; passwords are stored as SHA-256 + per-user random salt hashes (no plaintext), with constant-time comparison against timing side channels. Table-level privileges : GRANT <priv[,priv...]> ON <table> TO '<user>' / REVOKE ... FROM '<user>' ; priv ∈ {SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, ALL}; repeated GRANT/REVOKE are idempotent. Database-level & column-level privileges (M17) : GRANT/REVOKE <priv> ON DATABASE <db> TO/FROM '<user>' , GRANT/REVOKE <priv> ON <table> (<col>, ...) TO/FROM ... ; role-targeted grants. Role system (M17) : CREATE ROLE / DROP ROLE [IF EXISTS] / SHOW ROLES , GRANT ROLE '<role>' TO '<user>' / REVOKE ROLE ... FROM '<user>' , SHOW GRANTS FOR '<user>' . Aggregated privilege checks : table direct ∪ database ∪ role inheritance for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, plus column-level checks. Cascade cleanup : DROP USER / DROP TABLE / DROP ROLE automatically clean related grants to avoid dangling authorizations. Connection auth : the server supports optional connection auth (AUTH handshake); without it the connection runs as the default root user; when AllowLegacy is enabled legacy clients fall back to a restricted guest mode, or are rejected in strict mode.
docs.title: 6.3 RBAC & Privileges

docs.text: Audited events: connect, auth, DML, DDL, privilege events. Storage: ring buffer + JSON Lines persistence. Query: SHOW AUDITLOG ; hot switch: SET audit_log = on/off .
docs.title: 6.4 Audit Log (T30)

docs.text: openxdb doctor --data-dir ./data [--addr 127.0.0.1:7788] [--json] Checks: - Data directory & WAL integrity; - RocksDB open health; - m:tables / m:regions metadata consistency & route self-consistency; - Binlog readability & LSN (read-only PeekLastLSN ); - Optional online port/PING and slow-query checks. Output: human-readable or --json report; exit codes 0=pass / 1=warn / 2=error.
docs.title: 7.1 openxdb doctor Health Check (T20)

docs.text: openxdb stats [--addr 127.0.0.1:7788] [--interval 5] [--json] Metrics: active connections (server session counter), table count, region count & route distribution, slow query count, binlog LSN (optional two-sample growth via --interval ), table or --json output; backed by the SHOW STATS statement.
docs.title: 7.2 openxdb stats Live Metrics (T20)

docs.text: Metrics port: metrics_port (default 7790), exposing Prometheus-format metrics. Metrics source: same metrics.Snapshot data source (connections, table/region counts, slow queries, LSN, etc.).
docs.title: 7.3 Prometheus Metrics (M13)

docs.text: Threshold: default 100ms; SET slow_query_threshold = <ms> (<=0 disables recording). File logging: default <data_dir>/slow.log , configurable; SET slow_query_log = on/off hot switch. In-memory: keeps the most recent N records (default 64, adjustable via Engine.SetSlowQueryMax(n) ); query via SHOW SLOWQUERIES (newest first). Record fields: SQL text, user, start time, duration (ms), result rows (0 on failure), error message (empty on success). Low-overhead design: threshold check before formatting; normal statements incur zero formatting cost.
docs.title: 7.4 Slow Queries (M13)

docs.text: Rule model: metric / op / threshold / duration_sec / severity , stored as JSON. Configuration: SET / SET PERSIST alert_rules* . Evaluation engine: over the same metrics.Snapshot data source, NORMAL/ALERT/RESOLVED state machine + duration debounce. Notification: logx ring buffer + optional webhook / file channel. Management statements: SHOW ALERT RULES / SHOW ALERT STATUS / SHOW ALERTS . Evaluation loop wired to the database lifecycle.
docs.title: 7.5 Alert Rules (T37)

docs.text: Auto-split : the write path (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) accumulates per-table write counters after commits; at half the row threshold a real row-count check runs (scans the local region's physical key space); a local region exceeding the threshold is split in half along its data midpoint inside the same transaction (existing rows re-routed, route table replaced, metadata persisted). Manual split : SPLIT REGION (by data midpoint) or explicit boundaries. Manual balance : BALANCE (returns number of migrated regions; a second BALANCE returns 0). Auto balance : Engine.SetAutoBalance(enabled, interval) periodic trigger; compares local region counts with the least-loaded live node and migrates the largest region there. Online migration : source route unchanged during migration, reads/writes uninterrupted; scan source region rows → REGION_PUSH loads the target → switch local route and persist; other live nodes learn the new owner via the next heartbeat route sync. Single-node mode BALANCE reports cluster not enabled .
docs.title: 7.6 Region Split & Load Balancing (M7)

docs.text: Failure detection : heartbeat (PING/PONG, default 2s/6s) timeout → node marked down (OnDown callback). Automatic region re-assignment : regions owned by the down node are re-assigned to a live node (fullest replica scan + REGION_PUSH ), replacing manual ASSIGN REGION . Read failover : cross-node reads transparently re-route to the new owner (QUERY_REQ re-routed), no client error. Replication master failover : follower auto-promotes when the old master is down ( PromoteToMaster / EnableAutoFailover / StopAutoFailover ), keeping the write path available.
docs.title: 7.7 HA Failover (M6)

docs.text: Async replication (default) : master-follower; commit-hook binlog (independent append-only file, monotonically increasing LSN); replicator push with per-slot resume; follower idempotent apply; PING/PONG heartbeats with offline detection. Semi-sync replication : SET replication_mode = semi-sync ; waits for partial/full ACK (outside the transaction lock); degrades to async on ACK timeout or no slave. Sync replication : SET replication_mode = sync ; waits for all ACKs; refuses pseudo-sync when requirements cannot be met. Hot-switch config: SET replication_mode / SET replication_ack / SET replication_timeout .
docs.title: 8.1 Replication (M2 + T33)

docs.text: RegionInfo metadata persisted as m:regions ; Router with half-open [StartKey, EndKey) boundary semantics. Region-prefixed physical keys ( r + regionID:8B + inner key). Cross-region point/range/full-table queries via range expansion + merge. Management: SPLIT / LIST REGIONS / LOCATE REGION ; default single-region shape keeps pre-sharding behavior unchanged.
docs.title: 8.2 Sharding (M3)

docs.text: Node topology: NodeInfo (NodeID/Addr/Role master|follower/State active|down + last seen), node registry persisted to m:nodes , auto-restored on open. Management: ADD NODE '<addr>' / SHOW NODES ; openxdb start --cluster-addr <addr> starts cluster mode. Cluster route table: region → node; ASSIGN REGION <id> TO NODE '<nodeID>' updates ownership and pushes data; SHOW REGION ROUTES shows everything in one table. Cross-node reads: non-local regions are forwarded over TCP to their owning node and merged back; Local semantics (Node empty or equal to selfID) keep single-node deployments at zero regression.
docs.title: 8.3 Multi-Node Cluster (M4)

docs.text: Cross-node write atomicity: autocommit INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (incl. CSV IMPORT) touching both local and remote regions execute as two-phase commit. Flow: coordinator applies local ops → PREPAREs remote participants (ops persisted under m:2pc:* for crash recovery) → commits locally → idempotently COMMITs all participants. Failure semantics: any PREPARE failure or local commit failure ABORTs the whole statement; error codes TXN_PREPARE_FAILED / TXN_COMMIT_ABORTED / TXN_COMMIT_UNCERTAIN . Protocol frames 22-27 extend M4 framing; single-node deployments never enter the 2PC path (zero regression).
docs.title: 8.4 Distributed Write / 2PC (M5)

docs.text: Global Timestamp (TSO) : 64-bit physical-ms + 24-bit logical layout; strict monotonicity (clock-fallback safe); batch issuance (GetBatch allocates contiguous ranges, remote clients cache a batch to amortize RTT); transaction-boundary Reset drops unconsumed cache so a new snapshot reads from the authoritative sequence head. Distributed snapshot isolation : version records m:ver:<key>:<commit_ts> (key-first so per-key ranges stay contiguous); begin_ts/commit_ts globally comparable across nodes with cross-node passthrough. 2PC recovery hardening : coordinator persists CoordRecord ( m:2pc:coord:<txid> ), decides commit/abort on restart (RecoverCoordinated2PC), and idempotently drives participants to completion ( TXN_COMMIT_UNCERTAIN completion).
docs.title: 8.5 Distributed Transactions / TSO (M8)

docs.text: DDL metadata is broadcast to all online nodes via cluster DDL_PUSH frames; each node applies idempotently by TableID. Offline/apply-failure nodes record pending items, replayed before the next broadcast or via ReplayPendingDDL . Single-node zero-trigger compatibility; works alongside the T33 replication chain.
docs.title: 8.6 Cross-Node DDL (T34)

docs.text: See section 6.1 .
docs.title: 8.7 Distributed Backup Consistency (T35)

docs.text: Current throughput bottleneck: global session-lock serialization + per-statement round trips (each statement is exchanged between driver and server one by one). E5 also fixed a shared-session concurrency bug and completed arithmetic-expression / DISTINCT / DECIMAL-precision workarounds. Historical benchmark references: E3 SQL OLTP end-to-end 256.3 TPS (8:2) / 605.4 TPS (5:5); E4 stability 6-min mixed load 307–385 TPS without degradation, restart COUNT(*) == 150466; E2 fsync engine benchmark sync write 747k TPS seq / 198k rand (batch=1000), group-commit batch 181x vs per-key fsync. These are experiment records, not external commitments.
docs.title: 9.3 Bottleneck Notes

docs.text: For the full list see KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md (to be created). Summary: SQL subset : OpenXDB implements a SQL subset, not the full SQL standard. The HAVING clause is not supported; DDL/DML/query capabilities are as defined in Chapter 4 . Not MySQL wire protocol : uses a self-developed binary TCP protocol, so MySQL ecosystem tools (standard sysbench, official mysqldump client, etc.) cannot directly connect. Global session-lock performance boundary : the current serialized global session lock is the primary throughput bottleneck (see Chapter 9 ); high-concurrency write throughput is limited. Line protocol limits : cell newlines are unsupported (multi-line parameter strings are rejected by drivers); empty cells represent both NULL and empty string. Types & precision : DECIMAL is normalized to fixed 4 decimal places internally; in JSON export DECIMAL is approximated via strconv.ParseFloat (or kept as a string). Auth & legacy mode : without an AUTH handshake connections run as the default root user; legacy clients fall back to a restricted guest mode when AllowLegacy is enabled, or are rejected in strict mode. Stored procedures/triggers are a restricted subset : only the syntax and semantics defined in the design documents are supported; no full SQL/PL capabilities. Distributed statements limited in single-node mode : BALANCE and similar cluster statements explicitly report cluster not enabled ; cross-node writes require cluster mode. Distributed capability boundaries : cross-node writes rely on 2PC protocol frames; replication modes (async/semi-sync/sync) are switched via hot config; sync mode refuses pseudo-sync when ACKs cannot be satisfied. Import compatibility : mysqldump import is text-rule parsing covering a common dump syntax subset; unknown types error in strict mode and skip the table in lenient mode; cell parse failures drop the row in lenient mode.
docs.title: 10. Known Limitations & Boundaries

docs.text: Check that the CGO environment variables point to RocksDB: CGO_CFLAGS / CGO_CXXFLAGS → <rocksdb>/include , CGO_LDFLAGS → <rocksdb-build> -lrocksdb . On Windows add -lshlwapi -lrpcrt4 -lws2_32 (already in repository #cgo ). Prefer scripts/build.ps1 / scripts/build.sh for one-shot builds. Do not add undeclared flags such as -lstdc++ / -lz .

docs.text: SHOW USERS is implemented by identifier text matching; USERS is not in the keyword table, so CREATE TABLE users and SHOW USERS coexist without special handling. For other keyword conflicts, consult the parsing rules in the design documents.
docs.title: Q2: Table names colliding with keywords (e.g., users vs SHOW USERS)?

docs.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / DROP TABLE IF EXISTS / DROP USER IF EXISTS / DROP ROLE IF EXISTS succeed silently when the object does not exist; when it exists, normal semantics apply (create errors or drop succeeds).
docs.title: Q3: What is the idempotency semantics of IF NOT EXISTS?

docs.text: BACKUP TO '<path>' produces a single-file consistent-snapshot backup; RESTORE FROM '<path>' idempotently restores (same-named tables drop-then-recreate); for point-in-time recovery use RESTORE FROM '<path>' TO LSN <n> to replay binlog up to the target LSN. For distributed clusters use the T35 coordinator for multi-node consistent backup.
docs.title: Q4: How to back up and restore?

docs.text: Initialize each node with openxdb init --data-dir <dir> , then start in cluster mode with openxdb start --cluster-addr <addr> ; register peers with ADD NODE '<addr>' , assign region ownership with ASSIGN REGION <id> TO NODE '<nodeID>' , and inspect with SHOW NODES / SHOW REGION ROUTES .
docs.title: Q5: How to set up a cluster?

docs.text: JDBC: jdbc:openxdb://host:7788 ; Python: openxdb.connect("host", 7788) . Both drivers use the self-developed protocol with ? placeholders (client-side safe escaping). For TLS, configure certificate verification mode in JDBC and pass TLS connection parameters in Python.
docs.title: Q6: How do drivers connect?

docs.text: OpenXDB uses a self-developed binary TCP protocol ( pkg/server ), not MySQL wire protocol, so the official MySQL client cannot connect directly. Use the built-in REPL ( openxdb repl ) or the JDBC / Python drivers.

docs.text: Generate a certificate, then start with openxdb start --data-dir ./data --tls-cert cert.pem --tls-key key.pem (both flags required); TLS-only is the default with plaintext rejected; SET PERSIST tls_allow_legacy=on enables plaintext/TLS coexistence. Use --replica-tls for the replica port.
docs.title: Q9: How do I enable TLS?

docs.text: All performance numbers come from the E5 standard bench alignment experiment ( docs/experiments/E5_standard_bench_alignment.md ) with real measurements (8 threads × 60s / 120s, 0 errors). The current throughput bottleneck is global session-lock serialization + per-statement round trips; the project positions itself as a single-node edge benchmark — functional completeness first, performance optimization ongoing. This manual is compiled from the OpenXDB README.md and docs/ design documents, v1.0.0.

docs.text: OpenXDB 产品手册（中文版） ¶ 版本：v1.0.0 更新日期：2026-10-16 定位：单机端侧基准的关系型数据库内核。本文档所有功能与数据均来自 README.md 与 docs/ 目录下的真实设计文档，不包含任何臆造参数或数字。 目录 ¶ 产品简介与定位 快速开始 安装与部署 SQL 参考 客户端驱动 数据安全 运维与可观测 分布式能力 性能基准 已知限制与边界 FAQ 1. 产品简介与定位 ¶ OpenXDB 是一个 从零自研 的单机/分布式关系型数据库内核，使用 Go 语言编写，存储引擎基于 RocksDB（通过 cgo 薄桥接层接入）。内核完整包含 WAL（预写日志）、事务、SQL 解析与执行、复制、分片、2PC、HA（高可用）、备份恢复等能力，从教学与实验出发，逐步演进为具备分布式能力的完整内核。 1.1 定位边界 ¶ OpenXDB 使用 自研二进制 TCP 协议 （ pkg/server ）， 不是 MySQL wire protocol ，因此无法直接兼容 MySQL 生态工具（如标准 sysbench、mysqldump 之外的 binlog 工具等）。 性能定位为 单机端侧基准 ：当前内核实现了完整功能链路，性能优化仍在持续进行，实测吞吐数据见 第 9 章 。 不将 TiDB、TDSQL、MySQL 等作为对标对象，OpenXDB 是一个独立实现的内核，用于学习、实验与端侧场景。 1.2 核心能力 ¶ 能力 说明 存储引擎 RocksDB-backed KV 存储（cgo 桥接 pkg/storage/rocksdb ）+ 纯 Go 内存 B+Tree（ pkg/storage/btree ，作为参考实现与比较器） WAL 追加式预写日志，崩溃恢复重放（ pkg/wal ） 事务 本地 ACID 事务，快照隔离（snapshot isolation）；读己之写合并、墓碑、点/范围扫描（ pkg/txn ） SQL 子集 DDL/DML/查询/运维语句，详见 第 4 章 二级索引 创建时回填、DML 自动维护、等值/范围/ORDER BY 查询优化 复制 master-follower 异步复制（M2），支持 async / semi-sync / sync 三种模式（T33） 分片 逻辑分片：RegionInfo 元数据 + Router 半开区间 [StartKey, EndKey) + region 前缀物理键（M3） 多节点集群 节点拓扑、集群路由表（region → 节点）、跨节点 SELECT 转发与合并（M4） 分布式写 / 2PC 跨节点写原子性，两阶段提交（M5） HA / 故障转移 心跳故障检测、region 自动重指派、读 openxdb start --data-dir <dir> [--port 7788] 启动 TCP server（默认端口 7788） openxdb start --cluster-addr <addr> 以集群模式启动（节点 ID 由 --node-id 指定或自动生成） openxdb doctor 健康检查（退出码 0=通过 / 1=警告 / 2=错误） openxdb stats
